summary.summary: Rushmoor's unaudited 2025/26 accounts show £149m of borrowing — half of it maturing within 12 months, including £62m of short-term PWLB — against £28.7m of usable reserves, while the £110.6m commercial investment-property estate is written down further and £21.9m of assets sit in held-for-sale. The revenue outturn beat budget (only £2.4m of a budgeted £3.4m reserves drawdown was needed against an approved £5.2m budget gap), but the AGS discloses that external auditor EY has again raised concerns about the council's progress on financial sustainability and resolving its deficit, and is explicitly keeping a public interest report under consideration — on top of disclaimed audit opinions for every year from 2020/21 to 2023/24. Rushmoor is abolished into a new North Hampshire unitary from 1 April 2028 under local government reorganisation. For a lender the direction of travel is mixed: debt fell £17m in the year and the accounting deficit narrowed from £37.0m to £6.0m, but the balance sheet has not been independently verified for years and the auditor's sustainability warning is live.
summary.as_of_doc: Unaudited Statement of Accounts and Annual Governance Statement

signals.headline: Disclaimer audit opinions were issued for 2020/21, 2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24 under the audit reset, and EY still lack assurance over 2024/25 in-year movements and brought-forward balances (AGS, PDF p95)
signals.why: The balance sheet a lender relies on has gone unverified for four-plus years, so reported reserves and asset values carry extra uncertainty.

signals.headline: £2.4m was drawn from reserves in 2025/26 (vs £3.4m budgeted) against an approved £5.2m budget gap; earmarked reserves fell from £21.0m to £17.8m, and EY's 2024/25 annual report again raises concerns on financial sustainability and resolving the deficit, with a public interest report kept under review
signals.why: The revenue budget only balances with reserves, and the external auditor is formally warning about the trajectory — the strongest pre-distress marker short of statutory intervention.

signals.headline: £74.0m of £149.0m total borrowing matures within 12 months of 31 March 2026 — £62.0m short-term PWLB plus £12.0m from other local authorities (Note 21)
signals.why: Half the debt book must be repaid or refinanced inside a year at prevailing rates.

signals.headline: AGS flags quarterly monitoring of Farnborough International Ltd's trading and cashflow as a 'risk to the council', £750k of Rushmoor Development Partnership costs that would be funded from usable revenue reserve if written off, and a £0.8m contingent grant repayment if Civic Quarter conditions are not met by 31 March 2027 (PDF p95)
signals.why: Company and JV exposures could crystallise against reserves that are already funding the revenue gap.

signals.headline: Unaudited 2025/26 accounts published 30 June 2026 with EY's audit due to complete December 2026; the draft AGS followed on 1 July, one day after the statutory 30 June deadline
signals.why: Sets the audit clock for the first post-backlog opinion, and the missed AGS deadline is a minor statutory lapse worth tracking.

signals.headline: Total borrowing fell £17.0m in 2025/26, from £166.0m to £149.0m, and reduced borrowing interest costs were a named contributor to the £1.3m outturn saving
signals.why: Deleveraging from the commercial-property era trims refinancing needs and interest cost at the margin.

findings.paper_title: Budget Outturn, 2026-27 Q1 forecast and MTFS update - Report No. FIN2613
findings.headline: Service savings strategy abandoned; discovered significant savings could not be achieved without adversely affecting service delivery
findings.detail: The 2025/26 MTFS required recurring service reductions of £1.78m, increasing to £3.781m by 2027/28. A discovery phase concluded that 'significant savings or lower-priority services could not be readily identified without adversely affecting service delivery.' The council then ceased this savings strategy, switched to relying on reserves, and moved planned efficiencies to the North Hampshire Unitary Authority.
findings.matters: The council has abandoned sustainable cost-cutting and is instead treating short-term reserve depletion as its financial strategy, suggesting structural problems with its cost base.
findings.figures: 2025/26 required service reductions: £1.78m. Planned 2027/28 reduction: £3.781m (no longer pursued).
findings.quote: it ceased the service prioritisation savings strategy, maintained a no net budget growth approach other than unavoidable pressures, and planned to use reserves where necessary.

findings.paper_title: Budget Outturn, 2026-27 Q1 forecast and MTFS update - Report No. FIN2613
findings.headline: Council reserves will be drawn down to fund structural deficits, with estimated £2.253m available at Vesting Day before risks
findings.detail: The council budgeted for a £2.362m deficit in 2025/26 (now better at £2.362m from reserves). Going forward, it plans deficits of £442k in 2026/27 and £2.694m annually from 2027/28, to be met from reserves. Estimated available reserves at Vesting Day: £2.253m, but this is before accounting for the risks outlined (property income, receipts delays, Serco, LGR).
findings.matters: The council is structurally deficit and treating reserves as a funding source, not a contingency, with limited buffer remaining against the material risks identified.
findings.figures: 2025/26 outturn deficit: £2.362m. Reserves at 31 March 2026: £6.914m. Estimated at Vesting Day: £2.253m (before risks).
findings.quote: the estimated revenue reserves available to fund the forecast deficit at Vesting Day have increased from £1.828 million to £2.253 million before consideration of the risks outlined below.

findings.paper_title: Budget Outturn, 2026-27 Q1 forecast and MTFS update - Report No. FIN2613
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation costs expected to be significant but not yet budgeted in the MTFS
findings.detail: LGR cost apportionment methodology across Hampshire is still being assessed. Costs are expected to be significant and will place 'additional demands on available reserves.' While some may be funded through Flexible Use of Capital Receipts, 'a substantial proportion is expected to fall directly on the revenue budget.' No additional provision has been included in this MTFS update beyond existing assumptions.
findings.matters: A material unfunded cost burden is likely to emerge after this MTFS was set, putting further pressure on reserves and cashflow.
findings.figures: None quantified in the paper; costs still being assessed.
findings.quote: These costs are expected to be significant and will place additional demands on available reserves. While some expenditure may qualify for funding through the Flexible Use of Capital Receipts Direction, a substantial proportion is expected to fall directly on the revenue budget. No additional provision has been included within this MTFS update beyond existing assumptions.

findings.paper_title: Budget Outturn, 2026-27 Q1 forecast and MTFS update - Report No. FIN2613
findings.headline: Serco contract renegotiation concluding September 2026 with risk of cost pressures beyond current £1.095m budget
findings.detail: Contract negotiations conclude in September 2026. The council has provisioned £500k plus a further £595k in the current forecast. Under either the existing arrangement or a move to Twin Stream model, the council must procure and fund vehicles and equipment. The paper acknowledges 'risk of additional cost pressures arising beyond the current budget assumptions.'
findings.matters: A major service contract is being renegotiated with material uncertain costs that could exceed budget in either outcome scenario.
findings.figures: February 2026 provision: £500k. Additional assumed in current review: £595k. Total: £1.095m.
findings.quote: The Council will be able to either continue the existing contract arrangements or move to a Twin Stream service model. Under either option, the Council will be responsible for procuring and funding vehicles and equipment. There remains a risk of additional cost pressures arising beyond the current budget assumptions.

findings.paper_title: Budget Outturn, 2026-27 Q1 forecast and MTFS update - Report No. FIN2613
findings.headline: Audit of 2025/26 outturn not yet completed; adjustments could materially impact reported position and forecasts
findings.detail: The 2025/26 position reported in this paper is provisional. The council explicitly notes it 'has not yet achieved an unqualified audited financial position' and that audit adjustments could impact the reported outturn and forward financial forecasts. Any such impacts will be reflected in subsequent monitoring reports.
findings.matters: A lender cannot rely on the financial position stated here—the final audited outturn and any audit qualifications could reveal material issues not currently disclosed.
findings.quote: Given that the Council has not yet achieved an unqualified audited financial position, there remains a risk that adjustments arising from the completion of the audit process could impact the Council's reported financial position and future financial forecasts.
